precepts.text: Many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet, and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian. Christ himself reached back and referenced this exact history.
precepts.point: Who did the healing? The spirit of Christ, working through Elisha. What healed Naaman was his belief and his obedience to the word of the prophet.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Christ himself reached back and referenced this exact history. “I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land; But unto none of them was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow.”

Then the point: “And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.” Of all the lepers, the one cleansed was the one who humbled himself, believed, and went down and dipped seven times according to the saying of the man of God.

And seven also represents complete deliverance. Naaman dipped seven times and was delivered from his leprosy; Christ, the one whose spirit healed him through Elisha, spoke of it himself.

precepts.text: When the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season. You think Satan stopped tempting Christ? He never stopped; he just left for a season and came back in different ways. When Christ was about to be crucified, Satan came back, and he came back by jumping on Peter.
precepts.point: Satan comes for all of us. He comes different ways to defile us and destroy us: for some it is money, for some it is sex, for some it is hatred. Satan only comes at you at your weakness. So examine yourself: what is my weakness? That is what I need to strengthen, because that is what Satan is going to try to destroy me with. The worst brothers and sisters are the ones that say they have no weakness, that they are perfect; those are the ones dealing with the heaviest demons and just hiding it. Everybody has weakness. The Lord told Paul, my strength is made perfect in weakness; Paul asked three times for his weakness to be removed, and the Lord said no, fight it and become strong.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness

precepts.why:
Christ told the disciples he must go to Jerusalem, suffer, be killed and be raised again the third day. That was a good thing: he had to die to redeem the nation of Israel. But Peter took him and rebuked him: “Be it far from thee, Lord”. And Christ turned and said, “Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me”. What happened there? Satan literally jumped on Peter. That was not Peter; that was Satan talking to Christ through Peter, and Christ was talking to Satan.

Luke shows how that could be. After the temptation in the wilderness: “And when the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season.” For a season. You think Satan stopped tempting Christ? He never stopped. He just left for a season and kept coming in different ways. When Christ was about to be crucified, Satan came back, and he came by jumping on Peter.

That is why Christ told Peter in another place that Satan desired to have him, to sift him as wheat, but that he had prayed for him that his faith fail not.

Satan comes for all of us; that is his job. For some it is money, for some it is sex, for some it is hatred. He comes at your weakness. So examine yourself: what is my weakness? That is what you need to strengthen, because that is what Satan will try to destroy you with. The worst are the ones who say they have no weakness; they deal with the heaviest demons and are just good at hiding it. The war is in your mind: when the evil thought comes, rebuke it, as Christ did: get thee behind me.

precepts.text: Satan used Psalm 91 to say cast thyself down; Christ answered thou shalt not tempt the Lord, because the psalm is about the deliverance of Israel, not a dare.
precepts.point: Many that sleep in the dust shall awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame. They that be wise, who study, pray and apply, shine as the firmament. The book was sealed to the time of the end, so the open understanding coming out now shows we are in it, and knowledge has increased.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Psalm 91 promises the deliverance of Israel in the time of trouble: “He shall give his angels charge over thee”. Satan used that same psalm on Christ: “And he brought him to Jerusalem, and set him on a pinnacle of the temple, and said unto him, If thou be the Son of God, cast thyself down from hence”.

“For it is written, He shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee: And in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.” Satan twisted the psalm into a dare, telling Christ to jump.

“And Jesus answering said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.” Christ answered that way because the psalm is not a dare to test God. It is about the deliverance of Israel in the midst of Armageddon, when a thousand fall at our side and ten thousand at our right hand, and the angels bear us up.

precepts.text: The devil shows Christ all the kingdoms of the world and says the power and the glory of them is delivered unto him. When was it delivered? Genesis 3.
precepts.point: 'It shall bruise thy head' because Satan's seed, the Romans, crucified Christ. 'Thou shalt bruise his heel' is the Lord taking down Satan and his children.

note.label: Fighting Satan - the War Within

precepts.why:
Satan made his move on Adam through the weaker vessel, and God brought judgment on the serpent, the woman and the man. To the serpent: “Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field”. That is not about livestock. This is paradise; he is cursed above every creation God made there. And, “upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life”.

That one line says two things. Man was made from the earth, and Satan is a celestial being, so “all the days of thy life” means his days are numbered: he will be destroyed in the future for what he did. And eating dust means he is on the earth, and the Lord handed him power over it.

Luke shows it: “the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.” When was the power of this earth delivered to Satan? In Genesis 3, what we just read.

And he gave it to whom he would: first to Cain, and then to Esau, the so-called white man in these last days. That is why Esau is able to create all this technology.

Then comes the declaration of war: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Back then her seed was Abel, then Seth and the chosen lineage, and Satan’s seed was Cain and his descendants. Today her seed is the twelve tribes of Israel, and his seed is the so-called Caucasians, Edom. And “it shall bruise thy head”, because his seed, the Romans, crucified Christ. Then, “and thou shalt bruise his heel”: the Lord will take down Satan and his children. So when the Bible says to be soldiers of Jesus Christ, we fight Satan, his wicked thoughts and whispers, and we also fight his children, his physical counterpart.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
Obadiah speaks “concerning Edom”: the white man, the Caucasian, by his biblical name. “Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars”. They were so proud that they went to the moon and claimed it for their own, something they did not even create. They do not let other nations plant a flag there; they said, the Eagle has landed. And now one of their government says, we own the moon, why not Greenland? That is pride.

There is a reason behind it, and Luke shows it: “the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it. If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.”

This Edomite is prideful because he has the spiritual power of Satan rolling with him. That is who gave him the power to go to the moon and to make these weapons to destroy all of mankind. No brown nation on the earth came up with the invention to destroy everybody; that belongs solely to the white man, because Satan is behind him. That is who he made a covenant with, not the God of the Bible.

So when you see In God we trust on the money, know he is not talking about anybody in this Bible. The Psalm proves it: “The wicked, through the pride of his countenance, will not seek after God: God is not in all his thoughts.” “The wicked in his pride doth persecute the poor”, and you judge whether a man is prideful or humble by how he treats the lowly: the blacks, Hispanics and Native Indians, who have no army. Out of all the kingdoms, Assyrian, Babylonian, Persian, Greek, Roman, none has been more prideful than Esau.

But the kingdoms Satan gives are not the Lord's, and Obadiah answers the pride: “thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” From the moment they said the Eagle has landed, they have been going down, because that is when the Israelites started hitting the streets with the word of God. The more we are gathered together, the more Esau comes down.

precepts.text: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked.
precepts.point: Christ answered that he worships and serves God alone.

note.label: Political Power Under Darkness

precepts.why:
How did Esau get all this power? “And the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.” He showed Christ all the great kingdoms: America, Russia, China, France, Germany, Europe. “All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.” All these kingdoms were delivered to Satan, and he can give them to whoever he wants. But Christ answered, “Get thee behind me, Satan”, and worshipped God only. Satan tried to give Christ what already belonged to Christ.

Job shows who the power was given to: “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof”. We are the judges of the earth, and the wicked covered our faces. The scripture says the earth was created for the Israelites, so the earth belongs to us. Esau covered the faces of the judges, and now Esau tries to give us what actually belongs to us, and some of us fall for it.

“if not, where, and who is he?” If this man is not the devil, show me who is. When you look, the most evil things on planet earth were caused by the white man. Somebody said, you want peace on earth, get rid of the white man. Picture the peace this land had before the white man came here, the peace the so-called American Indians had among themselves, the peace the continent of Africa had before the white man docked his boat there. They brought disease, rape, murder and stealing. That is what Malachi 1 is talking about: everywhere you see evil, move the curtain, and the white man is right there.

But the triumphing of the wicked is short, and the joy of the hypocrite but for a moment. The kingdoms the devil gave him will be broken, and the God of heaven will set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed.

precepts.point: Israel shall be named priests of the Lord, receive double for its shame, and its seed shall be known among the Gentiles.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
Isaiah 61 is fulfilled in Christ, who read it himself: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor.” The good tidings of Isaiah are the gospel. And the poor are not everybody: “the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.” The poor are the poor of Zion. You do not even have to go to Isaiah 14; Isaiah 61 itself says it is them that mourn in Zion.

“he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives.” We are the captives. How can you read captive and think everybody? Rome was dominating Israel at that time. “and recovering of sight to the blind”: we are the blind people. “to set at liberty them that are bruised”: bruised in sin.

“To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.” The acceptable year of the Lord is our day of jubilee, and we had better accept that.

Imagine the Israelites and the Romans sitting in church together, the captives and the captors side by side, told we are all the same. It makes no sense. Jake looks over at Esau to see if he is upset, and if master is upset at this reading, he disregards it: black Christians hate anything that upsets white folks, and that is why they do not believe. But Christ read it plainly: he came to proclaim liberty to the captives of Israel, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound, bound in these prisons we call America, the Caribbean and whatever lands we are in.

precepts.text: All this power will I give thee, for that is delivered unto me.
precepts.point: They covet fields and take them by violence, and oppress a man and his house.

note.label: Babylon Speaks Plainly: Venezuela and the Real WMD

precepts.why:
“Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their beds! when the morning is light, they practise it, because it is in the power of their hand.” Upon their beds means they are insulated from consequence; they know nobody can touch them, like Trump saying in his first term he could shoot somebody on Fifth Avenue and nobody would do anything. When the morning is light, they do it through institutions, laws and bills stacked higher than a ream of paper, with billions in them for Israel and Ukraine. They are vessels of wrath fitted for destruction, and that is our hope: all that wrath will be paid back to them double.

Why is it in the power of their hand? Luke shows who gave it. After showing Christ all the kingdoms, “the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.”

To whomsoever I will, I give it. So who gave them their power? Satan. And who are the ministers of Satan? Babylon the great, Esau: what the world ignorantly calls the white man.

That is why they covet fields, oil fields, iron ore fields, rare earth fields, agricultural fields, and take them by violence, as with Venezuela. The power in their hand was delivered to them by the devil.

precepts.text: The devil offered Christ all the power and glory of the kingdoms for worship; the same spirit offered Balaam honor through Balak.
precepts.point: We are not to be ignorant of his devices, lest he get an advantage of us. Many are falling to those devices at home in this quarantine, letting the old man rise back up; resist the devil and he will flee, but give in and he will use you until he destroys you.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
The same spirit that offered Balaam honor through Balak tried the same device on Christ. “And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it. If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.”

All the power and the glory of the kingdoms in exchange for worship, as great honour was offered Balaam in exchange for cursing Israel. “And Jesus answered and said unto him, Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.”

Satan is an old spirit using the same tricks from the beginning of time: promotion by honor, riches, prestige, and lust.

precepts.point: Who blesses everybody that does not keep the commandments and still gets everything they desire? Satan says come as you are; whoever wants power, fame, and money in this world without obeying God can have it from him, and you will pay the piper when you meet Christ. Share these precepts with your family.

note.label: Deuteronomy 8: Keep the Commandments and Live

precepts.why:
“And the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it. If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.”

Who blesses everybody that does not keep the commandments and still gets everything they desire? Satan says come as you are. Whoever wants power, fame and money in this world without obeying God can have it from him, and you will pay the piper when you meet Christ.

Here is Christianity wrapped up in a few scriptures: “thou say in thine heart, My power and the might of mine hand hath gotten me this wealth.” They keep no commandments and then boast, look what we have done, look at this job, look at all this stuff, as if the Most High gave them that power. But “it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant”. The power to get wealth belongs to the covenant; if you forget God and keep no commandments, it was not God blessing you. Share these precepts with your family.

precepts.text: The devil told Christ all this power and glory is delivered unto him to give to whomsoever he will, so the wicked prospering without keeping the commandments shows whom they worship.
precepts.point: Man being in honor abides not; he is like the beasts that perish, boasting himself and naming things after himself but destined to die.

note.label: Psalm 49: The Vanity of Riches Against the Grave

precepts.why:
The devil told Christ, “All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.” The power and glory of this world are delivered to the devil, and he gives them to whom he will. So when the wicked prosper without keeping the commandments, it shows who they worship.

That is who is behind the ones whose inward thought is that “their houses shall continue for ever”, who “call their lands after their own names”. The so-called white man names America after Amerigo Vespucci and names boulevards after dead men, thinking it will always be here for his children. But the Most High will take it from them, and everything returns to its natural name. Man being in honour abideth not; he is like the beasts that perish.

precepts.point: He is sent to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord and the day of vengeance of our God, to comfort all that mourn, and to give them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, and the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness, that they might be called trees of righteousness.

note.label: Isaiah 61: The Spirit of the Lord God Is Upon Me

precepts.why:
“The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound”. Christ quoted this passage when he read in the synagogue: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised”.

He applied the anointing to preach the gospel to himself. The anointed one of Isaiah 61, sent to the meek and the brokenhearted, to the captives and them that are bound, is Christ. He is the one sent to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord and the day of vengeance of our God, to comfort all that mourn, and to give beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning and the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness, that they might be called trees of righteousness.

precepts.text: When the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season.
precepts.point: The devil leaves him and angels come and minister unto him. The leaving is not permanent.

note.label: Matthew 4: The Temptation in the Wilderness and the Calling of the Fishers

precepts.why:
“Then the devil leaveth him, and, behold, angels came and ministered unto him.” Luke tells how long that leaving lasts: “And when the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season.”

The leaving is not permanent. He departed for a season, having ended all the temptation for that time, and he would be back. So it is with the temptations of the flesh, the eyes and pride: the devil goes away when he is answered with the word, but only for a season.

precepts.text: The verse he went back to, written to Israel in the wilderness.
precepts.point: He answers with the law: man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.

note.label: Luke 4: The Temptation and the Reading at Nazareth

precepts.why:
Full of the Holy Ghost, Christ was led by the Spirit into the wilderness, forty days tempted of the devil, and ate nothing. When the devil said “If thou be the Son of God, command this stone that it be made bread”, he answered with the law: “It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.”

This is the verse he went back to, written to Israel in the wilderness: “And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Lord doth man live.” Israel was humbled and suffered to hunger in the wilderness so they would learn that lesson; Christ, hungering in the wilderness, stood on it. Man lives by every word out of the mouth of the Lord, and Christ answered the devil with that word.

precepts.text: Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, and serve him, and shalt swear by his name.
precepts.point: Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve. Again the answer is a commandment.

note.label: Luke 4: The Temptation and the Reading at Nazareth

precepts.why:
The devil showed him “all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.” No man can do that, which settles who was standing there. Then the offer: “All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it. If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.” The offer is real, and the price is worship.

“Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.” Again the answer is a commandment, and this is the one: “Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, and serve him, and shalt swear by his name.” The Lord thy God is the one to fear and serve, him only. Christ would not take the kingdoms of the world at the price of breaking that commandment, and he put the devil behind him with it.
